That makes it the best fit for the one available slot under a sustainable-qualified-revenue objective, with activation_messaging (memory_91) and signup simplification (memory_31) as adjacent support rather than competitors for the slot. I am deliberately not chasing the competitor with promotional_pricing even though memory_73 looks like a direct match: discount-led acquisition of price-sensitive SMBs is the classic case where a short-window revenue lift converts into structurally lower-quality revenue (margin erosion, discount-anchored renewals, elevated churn after the promo period), which is a downstream value risk against the stated objective. I am spending both verification pulls on the two records that would actually change my decision. memory_73 because it is the option I am declining and the one whose consolidated summary most likely dropped caveats about measurement window, churn follow-up, and whether 'revenue lift' was gross or net of discount. memory_86 because it is the option I intend to run and I need to know the true effect size, whether 'completion' was measured as a downstream activation/retention outcome or just funnel throughput, and whether shortening onboarding removed qualification steps that feed pipeline quality (memory_44 suggests enterprise pipeline quality depends on richer, sales-assisted paths, so a blanket onboarding cut could quietly degrade lead qualification). Important caveat on my own inputs: every item here is a consolidated summary from archived sources, days 12-61, and consolidation strips confidence intervals, sample sizes, and null results.
